# ax-output

One result, two renderings: `--json` prints the data, text prints what the command's text() makes of the same data. Long results are cut predictably, and lists page with a cursor, so an agent can read a long answer in pieces.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add ourostack/ouro-ui/ax-output#v1.3.0
```

It installs `lib/ouro/ax/output.ts`. Its tests are `ax-output-tests`. Every item runs on Node 22.18 or later as it is copied: the files import each other as `./<file>.ts`. The [Ouro AX guide](../guides/ax.md) shows how they fit together.

## Exports

### `emptyText`

The text for a list that came back empty: what is empty, by the filter that emptied it ("Nothing unread."), never "nothing held yet" when the filter is why, then the command to run next. A tool's voice may add its `empty` line after.

```ts
function emptyText(what: string, next?: { command: string; why: string; } | undefined): string
```

### `page`

One page of a list. The cursor is the next item's offset, so it is stable while the list is.

```ts
function page<T>(items: readonly T[], options: { limit: number; cursor?: string | null | undefined; }) => Page<T>
```

### `Page`

```ts
interface Page<T> {
  items: T[];
  total: number;
  nextCursor: string | null;
}
```

### `render`

What stdout gets for a result: the JSON document, or the text. Always one trailing newline.

```ts
function render<R>(result: R, options: { json: boolean; text?: ((result: R) => string) | undefined; }) => string
```

### `truncate`

Cuts text to at most `max` characters at a line break where it can, and says so on its last line with how to get the rest.

```ts
function truncate(text: string, max: number, more?: string): Truncated
```

### `Truncated`

```ts
interface Truncated {
  text: string;
  truncated: boolean;
  total: number;
}
```
